Extract per-parameter posterior draws from a model fit

Source: R/fb_as_draws_simple.R
fb_as_draws_simple.Rd

S3 generic that extracts a named list of numeric posterior-draw vectors from a fit, keyed by the engine's own parameter names. The methods that reach an active engine are flexybayes_brms and flexybayes_inla. The brmsfit method reads a brms fit inside a flexyBayes fit, a two-part non-linear fit from fb_refit() under the names of the linear model. User-defined methods can extend the generic.

Usage

fb_as_draws_simple(fit, ...)

# S3 method for class 'flexybayes_inla'
fb_as_draws_simple(fit, n_samples = 1000L, ...)

# S3 method for class 'flexybayes_brms'
fb_as_draws_simple(fit, ...)

# S3 method for class 'brmsfit'
fb_as_draws_simple(fit, ...)

# Default S3 method
fb_as_draws_simple(fit, ...)

Arguments

fit

A model fit object carrying a posterior, dispatched on by the methods listed above.

...

Method-specific arguments: n_samples for the INLA method. The brms method returns every stored draw and refuses n_samples with method_argument_not_supported.

Value

A named list of numeric vectors, one element per parameter, each element holding that parameter's posterior draws.

Details

On an INLA fit the draws come from the fitted approximation: each draw takes one of INLA's hyperparameter configurations, chosen with its posterior weight, and draws the latent field from that configuration's Gaussian approximation, as INLA::inla.posterior.sample() does. Every random number comes from R's generator, so set.seed() before the call makes the draws repeatable.

Examples

# A named list of draw vectors, with no posterior dependency.
# \donttest{
if (requireNamespace("INLA", quietly = TRUE)) {
  set.seed(1)
  d <- data.frame(y = rnorm(60), x = rnorm(60), g = factor(rep(1:6, 10)))
  fit <- flexybayes(y ~ x + (1 | g), data = d, backend = "inla",
                    verbose = FALSE)
  dr <- fb_as_draws_simple(fit)
  names(dr)
}
